P-ALLOC-1.description: The modeled router calculates each active module’s capacity from its target share and available headroom. Inactive modules receive no additional capacity. For successful execution under the stated storage, memory and arithmetic conditions, the resulting allocation and capacity lists match the independent mathematical specification.
P-ALLOC-1.model: Source execution model with a Verity external-call interpretation
covered: Storage-backed module reads, response-dependent calls and checked calculations follow the modeled source order.
Successful capacity calculations match the independent capacity specification and produce the corresponding memory arrays.
The Verity call interpreter matches the producer’s return or error and module-call observations; static calls preserve its world.
missing: The compiler interpretation of memory operations and the effects of omitted internal writes remain assumptions.
The bound of 32 modules is derived only for the modeled initialization and update histories; migration and other histories remain outside that result.
The result does not establish equivalence with compiled or deployed bytecode.
conditions: Compiler interpretation of aligned, non-overlapping observed word loads/stores and copies; omitted private cache/configuration/scratch writes obey the stated frame and cache-field relations.

P-ALLOC-2.description: The modeled router calculates module capacities, distributes the requested deposits using the proportional allocation algorithm and converts the resulting allocations to wei. Under the stated conditions, the complete modeled calculation matches the independent mathematical specification.
P-ALLOC-2.model: Source execution model with a Verity module-call interpretation; the linked library call is recorded, not executed in the VM

P-RESERVE-1.description: For the specified queue and recipient behavior, successful withdrawals in the modeled Lido path preserve the withdrawal reserve. Failed withdrawals restore the modeled transaction state. These results depend on the stated configuration, storage, arithmetic and funding conditions.
P-RESERVE-1.model: Source transaction interpreter using Verity physical contract storage; not a full Verity EVM execution theorem
covered: Withdrawal correspondence covers ordered status and permission checks, live queue and frame reads, partition arithmetic and recipient effects.
The specified physical queue, consensus and recipient pipeline preserves the independent protected reserve on success.
The withdrawal specification restores the pre-transaction world on failure; attempted calls remain observable.
missing: Reserve protection does not cover arbitrary successful callbacks.
The transaction interpreter uses Verity contract storage, but full correspondence with Verity EVM execution and deployed callees is not established.
Sequence results cover only the modeled transitions, not every queue writer, migration or report path.
conditions: Compiler interpretation of aligned, non-overlapping observed word loads/stores and copies; omitted private cache/configuration/scratch writes obey the stated frame and cache-field relations.
